questions.question: The Indian Forest Act 1927 was enacted after repealing which of the following Indian forest acts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Forest Act, 1878.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was enacted after repealing the Indian Forest Act, of 1878.**
 
• **Indian Forest Act, 1927**__
 __
 
• The Indian Forest Act, of 1927- was enacted to consolidate the law related to forest, the transit of forest produce, and the duty liable on timber and other forests produced.
 
• The preamble to the Indian Forest Act, of 1927 states that the Act seeks to consolidate the law relating to forests, the transit of forest produce and the duty that can be levied on timber and other forest produce.
 
• It was largely based on previous Indian Forest Acts implemented under the British. Indian Forest Act of 1878 was the most famous one.
 
• The Indian Forest Act, 1927 was enacted after repealing the Indian Forest Act, 1878 for the purpose of consolidating the law relating to forests, the transit of forest produce and the duty leviable on timber and other forest produce.
 
 
 
• **Indian Forest Act, 1878**__
 __
 
• This act repealed the Indian forest act of 1865.
 
• This act was an extension of the government policy of establishing control over forests.
 
• It also made several provisions for the imposition of duties on timber.
 
• The basic aim of the act was to remove local rights in the reserved forest and keep them exclusively as Government reserves.
 
• The 1878 act divided forests into three categories.
 

 
 
• Reserved forests. 
 
• Protected forests.
 
• Village forests. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Forest Act, 1865**__

 
 
• The Indian Forest Act of 1865 extended British colonialism in India and claimed over forests in India.
 
• It empowered the British government to declare any land covered with trees as a government forest and make rules to manage it.
 
• It was a precursor to the Indian Forest Act of 1878.

questions.question: Which of the following plant hormones regulates growth, particularly by stimulating cell elongation in stems?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Auxin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stem Elongation**__

 __
 
• Stem elongation refers to the rapid growth in the length of the internodes of the upper stem before the reproductive phase starts for the plant.
 
• Stem elongation causes many problems for the plant, such as skinny stems that are too weak to support large flowers, as well as plants that grow too high vertically and appear spindly, so it should be prevented.
 
 
 
• **Auxin**__
 __
 
• Auxin is a group of plant hormones that regulate growth, particularly by stimulating cell elongation in stems.
 
• Auxins also play a role in cell division and differentiation, in fruit development, in the formation of roots from cuttings, in the inhibition of lateral branching and in leaf fall.
 
• The most important naturally occurring auxin is **ß- indolyl acetic acid (IAA).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethylene**__

 __
 
• Ethylene is the first-identified plant hormone known to regulate numerous processes in plant growth, development, and response to biotic and abiotic stresses.
 
• Ethylene is best known for its effect on fruit ripening and thus has great commercial importance in agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Gibberellin**__
 __
 
• Gibberellin is a group of plant hormones that occur in seeds, young leaves, and roots.
 
• It stimulates the growth of main stems, especially when applied to the whole plant.
 
• It is commercially obtained from fungi.
 
 
 
• **Cytokinin**__
 
 
• Cytokinins are plant hormones that influence not only numerous aspects of plant growth, development and physiology, including cell division.
 
• Cytokinins are also produced by other prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms such as bacteria, fungi, microalgae and insects.

questions.question: What do you call the property of an organism of self-regulation and the tendency to maintain a steady state within an external environment which is liable to change?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Homeostasis.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Homeostasis**__ 

 __
 
• Homeostasis refers to the body's need to reach and maintain a certain state of equilibrium.
 
• The term was first coined by a physiologist named Walter Cannon in 1926.
 
• Homeostasis is the body's tendency to monitor and maintain internal states, such as temperature and blood sugar, at fairly constant and stable levels.
 
• It is necessary because the body cells need to have suitable conditions around them for proper functioning.
 
• The excretory system works on the principle of homeostasis in a way that all wastes or unneeded substances are removed by the body.
 
• It is just like the thermostat in your house.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Consciousness**__

 __
 
• Consciousness is sentience or awareness of internal and external existence.
 
• It refers to your individual awareness of your unique thoughts, memories, feelings, sensations, and environments.
 
• Changes to consciousness can also result in changes in perception, thinking, understanding, and interpretations of the world.
 
 
 
• **Metabolism**__
 __
 
• Metabolism is the process by which your body converts what you eat and drink into energy.
 
• Its purpose is the conservation of food to building blocks for proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and some carbohydrates, and the elimination of metabolic wastes.
 
 
 
• **Irritability**__
 
 
• It is a characteristic of living organisms in being aware of and being able to respond to a stimulus that tends to disturb the steady-state or homeostasis which all organisms prefer for maintaining life.
 
• The most common scenario is distant dermatitis in a patient with a chronic eczematous leg ulcer.

questions.question: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India shall a Money Bill not be introduced in a Legislative Council?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 198.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 198**__ 

 __
 
• A Money Bill shall not be introduced in a Legislative Council, It can be presented in the Legislative Assembly only.
 
• No money bill can be introduced in the Legislative Assembly of a State, except on the recommendations of the Governor of the state.
 
• After a Money Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State having a Legislative Council, it shall be transmitted to the Legislative Council for its recommendations, and the Legislative Council shall within a period of fourteen days from the date of its receipt of the Bill return the Bill to the Legislative.
 
• Assembly with its recommendations and the Legislative Assembly may thereupon either accept or reject all or any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council.
 
• If the Legislative Assembly accepts any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council, the Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses with the amendments recommended by the Legislative Council and accepted by the Legislative Assembly.
 
• If the Legislative Assembly does not accept any of the recommendations of the Legislative Council, the Money Bill shall be deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form in which it was passed by the Legislative Assembly without any of the amendments recommended by the Legislative Council.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 333**__

 __
 
• Article 333 empowers the governor to nominate one Anglo-Indian to state assembly if he thinks it is not adequately represented.
 
 
 
• **Article 189**__
 
 
• Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies and quorum.

questions.question: ______ boundaries occur when plates collide and one plate is pushed under the other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convergent.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Convergent Boundaries**__

 __
 
• When two tectonic plates move toward each other and collide, they form a convergent plate boundary.
 
• There are three types of convergent plate boundaries: oceanic-oceanic boundaries, oceanic-continental boundaries, and continental-continental boundaries. Each one is unique because of the density of the plates involved.
 
• Convergent plate boundaries are often the sites of earthquakes, volcanoes, and other significant geological activity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Divergent boundaries**__

 __
 
• A divergent boundary occurs when two tectonic plates move away from each other.
 
• The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is an example of divergent plate boundaries.
 
 
 
• **Transform**__
 
 
• Transform boundaries are places where plates slide sideways past each other.
 
• Transform boundaries are found on the seafloor, where they connect segments of diverging mid-ocean ridges.

questions.question: When a river originates from a hill and flows in all directions, the drainage pattern is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radial.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Radial Pattern**__

 __
 
• The tributaries from a summit follow slope downwards and drain down in all directions.
 
• The radial drainage pattern develops around a central elevated point and is common to conically shaped features such as volcanoes.
 
• Examples: Streams of the Saurashtra region, the rivers originating from the Amarkantak Mountain, Central French Plateau, Mt. Kilimanjaro.
 
• The Narmada, Son and Mahanadi originate from Amarkantak Hills and flow in different directions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dendritic**__

 __
 
• This is an irregular tree branch shaped pattern that develops in a terrain that has uniform lithology and where faulting and jointing are insignificant.
 
• Examples: Indus, Godavari, Mahanadi, Cauvery, Krishna.
 
 
 
• **Trellis**__
 __
 
• In this type of pattern, the short subsequent streams meet the mainstream at right angles, and differential erosion through soft rocks paves the way for tributaries.
 
• Examples: The old folded mountains of the Singhbhum and Seine and its tributaries in the Paris basin have drainage of trellis pattern.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal**__
 
 
• In a low-lying basin, the streams converge from all sides.
 
• Examples: Streams of Ladakh, Tibet, and the Baghmati and its tributaries in Nepal.

questions.question: The area served by a canal system through supply of water for irrigation and other purposes is called a ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Command area.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Command Area**__

 __
 
• The area over which canal irrigation water flows by gravity is known as the command area.
 
• Types of Command areas in irrigation:
 
 
• **Gross Command Area**:
 
 
• It is the total area that can be economically irrigated from an irrigation scheme without considering the limitations of water.
 
• It is denoted by GCA.
 
• GCA= CCA + Uncultivable area 
 
 
 
• **Culturable Command Area**:
 
 
• A culturable area is an area in which a crop is grown at a particular time or crop season.
 
• It is denoted by CCA.
 
• CCA= GCA - Uncultivable area
 
 
 
• **Net Command Area**
 
 
• It is the Culturable Command Area obtained after the deduction of canal networks, supply ditches, etc constructed in the field.
 
• It is denoted by NCA.
 
• NCA= CCA - the area occupied by canals, networks, and ditches.
 
 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Irrigation**__

 
 
• Irrigation is supplying water artificially to the soil for the purpose of agricultural production.
 
• It is used in dry areas and during periods of inadequate rainfall.

questions.question: Muhammad Ghori attacked Tabarhinda (Bhatinda) in 1191, a strategic point for ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prithviraj Chauhan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1191 Muhammad Ghori attacked and captured Bhatinda, a part of Prithviraj dominion.
 
• This led Muhammad to come into a direct clash with Prithviraj Chauhan one of the most powerful Rajput rulers.
 
• It is known as the First Battle of Tarain.
 
• Muhammad Ghori was defeated in the battle and also wounded in the arm. The Muslim army was routed and the battle was completely won over by the Rajputs.
 
• **Prithviraj Chauhan**__
 __
 
• He was an Indian king from the Chahamana(Chauhan) dynasty.
 
• From the early years, Prithviraj Chauhan showed his sharpness and brilliance by learning all military skills.
 
• It was believed he mastered the skills of aiming the target based on its sound, known as the "Shabhbhedi" technique.
 
• His grandfather Angam, the ruler of Delhi, declared him the heir to the throne of Delhi.
 
• His defeat at Tarain is seen as a landmark event in the Islamic conquest of India and has been described in several semi-legendary accounts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Ghori**__

 
 
• He was the founder of a Muslim ruler in India. He ruled from 1173 to 1206.
 
• He is known to have started the Slave Dynasty and was the first of the Five sultanates which ruled Delhi before the Mughals.
 
• It was the second Battle of Tarain which opened the Delhi area to Muhammad Ghori. In 1192 AD, he invaded again after the 1191 AD invasion with more soldiers and weapons. He defeated Prithvi Raj Chauhan and captured Delhi.
 
• He was a Sunni Muslim who was instrumental in establishing Islamic supremacy in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• In 1206, He was murdered and his kingdom in northern India was left in the control of his general Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution demarcates the powers of the Union and the States, that is Union List, State List and Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh Schedule.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seventh Schedule__**

 __
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India defines and specifies the allocation of powers and functions between States and the Union.
 
• The Schedule contains three lists - Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• The Union List originally had 97 subjects. Now it has 100 subjects.
 
• The State List has 61 subjects now, It had 66 subjects initially. State legislatures can make laws on the subjects mentioned in this list.
 
• The Concurrent List has 52 subjects enumerated under it. Both the State as well as the Central Government can make laws mentioned on this list.
